answer: We define a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds enforce a bridge between identity verification and stake weight, precluding illicit entry via an inlet of multiple pseudonymous nodes. Subgame-perfect punishment matrices calibrate slashing penalties to exceed the capital return of sybil expansion, ensuring the vine of cascading rewards withers under scrutiny. By leveraging zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions, we prove that identity multiplication yields negative expected utility, driving the system to a robust Nash equilibrium.
